_comment: Per-cart manifest for the bundled roguelike. See docs/VOXBOX_ROGUE_PLAN.md.
name: deeper (bundled)
controls: cast the held scroll (on the title screen: torchlight on/off)
your torch burns down: find oil before it does
armour is the second bar: it subtracts from every hit you take
health comes back slowly in a fight, quickly once nothing is hunting you
bread and draughts heal; reaching a new floor heals more
bump a statue to read it; shrines work once each
scrolls ask before you take them: x yes, z no
corridors are places too, and things live in them
_camera: Three-quarter isometric: 12 degrees of azimuth and 38 of elevation. The elevation is what shows the floor plan; the azimuth is deliberately modest rather than the textbook 45, because the HUD and all the dialogue are drawn on a y-slice and a slice seen at 45 degrees skews the 3x5 font past comfortable reading. Framing was solved numerically rather than eyeballed: project the eight corners of a full-grid node, translate the camera along its own right/up axes until that box is centred, then shrink fov until it just fits. The first hand-tuned camera used 83 percent of the width and was off-centre enough to clip one edge while wasting the other; this uses 96 percent of the width and 89 of the height.
_groundZ: Pinned to the floor slab. Auto-derivation would work in a plain room, but a node full of pillars and sill walls shifts the mode of the topmost voxels and the drop shadows jump between rooms. Pinning keeps hero and monster shadows on the floor where they belong.
_lighting: Torchlight can be switched off from the title screen with z, and the choice is remembered in cartdata slot 2. Flat mode forces every light cell to one level, so the room is evenly lit and the pools disappear -- and the light map collapses from ~590 run-length boxes to 3, which makes it a performance option as well as a legibility one. The Pot Helm's -2 vision joke is inert while it is off.
_persistGlobals: hiscore and best_depth go through cartdata/dget/dset. A mid-run resume would only need run_seed and depth, since the dungeon regenerates from its seed, but permadeath is the point.
_config: Arrives in the cart as the CONFIG global, installed before the chunk loads (host.js, luaLiteral). persistGlobals carries numbers out of a cart and back in; this is the other direction, and it carries tables and strings. Everything here is an override: the cart holds its own defaults and runs identically with no manifest at all, so dropping deeper.lua on the page alone still works. tools/cartlab.py installs the same block, so the harnesses test the text that actually ships.
_config_textures: Per-flagstone mottling of walls and floors -- a plus/minus one nudge to the light level from an arithmetic hash, so it reads in every ramp rather than fighting the torchlight (VOXBOX_ROGUE_PLAN 2.1b). Off by default while the look is undecided: it also drops the floor's run count, since a flat-lit stretch collapses to one box again. Masonry banding and flagstone seams are structure, not texture, and are not affected.
_config_monuments: Statue and shrine text, the one part of the cart that is pure content. Statues are text only, so the list can grow as long as you like for nothing. A shrine also names a kind, and only the five the cart implements do anything: heal (+8 health), torch (refills the torch), arm (repairs the worst piece you are wearing), whet (a point back on the weapon slot, if you carry one), gold (a handful of coins). An unrecognised kind still speaks and is still spent once -- it just has no effect -- so a typo degrades rather than crashes. Both fields are drawn in the HUD banner: names and lines are written to 24 characters, which is what fits a row on the back plane beside the minimap column, and the font is A-Z 0-9 and ! " ' ( ) + , - . / : ? _ (runtime/js/font.js). Anything else advances the cursor and draws nothing.
_config_fx: Every visual flourish, as a named flag. Each one exists because something was measurably wrong without it, so they all default on except `textures`, which is still on trial -- turn any of them off to see what it was doing. textures: per-flagstone mottling of walls and floors (VOXBOX_ROGUE_PLAN 2.1b). wall_floor: walls never fall below light level 1, because index 1 of every ramp is the same navy and an unlit wall was literally the same colour as the unlit floor in front of it, leaving the room with no shape at all outside the torch pools. jitter: perturbs the squared distance per cell so light pools have ragged edges instead of compass-drawn arcs -- dithering the boundary would have been the textbook answer and would have wrecked the two RLE passes, since a checkerboard has no runs. hero_crest: two voxels of pink on the hero's head in a fixed colour the light map never touches, because everything else about him is drawn from the same ramps as a statue. arches: a lintel over each far-wall doorway, so exits are visible from across a dark room. liquid: water cycles its ramp along a travelling sine, drawn over the floor's cached runs rather than inside them. decals: blood and scorch stay where they were made for the life of the floor, lit like everything else so a stain in the dark is invisible. dissolve: rooms assemble over eight frames on entry instead of cutting in. damage_numbers: the number prints in the world on the target's own y-slice, which is exact rather than a guess at a projection the cart cannot do. theme_torches: each depth's torch pools use their own ramp -- all five themes named the same orange before, which switched off half the point of having two ramps per theme.

statues.say: HE RAN OUT ON THIS SPOT
